title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a duck in Austin, Texas, while operating in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present. The vehicle did not slow down or stop before hitting the animal. This represents a failure in object detection and response, where the system either did not recognize the duck as an obstacle or did not generate a stopping command.

A human safety operator was in the vehicle during autonomous operation but did not intervene to prevent the collision. It is not established whether the operator could have prevented the incident or what information was available to them at the time.

Avride's subsequent decision to exclude certain streets from its service area and to evaluate technology improvements through simulation suggests the company identified detection or response capabilities as needing refinement. Whether the improvements will adequately address similar animal-related scenarios in deployment remains unknown.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community backlash. The self-driving car, which was in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present, hit the duck without slowing down or stopping. The duck was well-known to residents, as it had been nesting in a pot outside a local Italian restaurant, and neighbors have since collected its eggs and placed them in an incubator.

Following the incident, Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating autonomously and investigated claims that it failed to stop at a stop sign, finding no evidence to support this allegation. The company has since adjusted its testing operations by excluding certain streets around the lake from its service area. Avride stated it is evaluating potential technology improvements to avoid similar incidents in the future through controlled simulation experiments, ensuring any changes do not compromise vehicle safety performance.
